request.description: Characterize official-range inverse-kinematic feasibility, joint-limit margins, Jacobian conditioning, compiled MuJoCo inertial/actuator quantities, and short full-control torque responses.
request.rationale: The initial decision is whether the first intervention should target geometric branch/limit selection or closed-loop settling authority. A dense official-range grid tests whether any target is infeasible or angle/radius localized, while compiled dynamics and multi-configuration torque probes quantify the authority available to arrest motion at the 50 Hz control interval. This evidence is more decision-relevant than an unstratified initial training result.

request.current_goal_gap: No learned candidate or behavioral success evidence exists. The remaining gap is to determine whether a policy can use the available torque authority to reach and stabilize across the full 0.06-0.20 m official radius range, and to allocate failures between post-entry settling, branch/limit selection, maneuver duration, and distribution shift.
request.current_synthesis: Observation from completed operation M1: a 2,088-point official-range grid found at least one joint-limit-valid inverse-kinematic branch for every target. The valid branch fraction was 0.9444, the minimum best-branch joint-limit margin was 12.33 degrees, and the minimum valid-branch Jacobian singular value was 0.0415. Compiled MuJoCo dynamics contain nonzero geom-derived masses and inertias, retain the authored 0.002 s timestep, 0.5 damping, 0.01 armature, and 5.0 actuator gear. Full-control open-loop probes produced initial joint accelerations of about 393-483 rad/s^2 and joint velocities of about 5.3-6.0 rad/s after ten 0.002 s substeps. These observations weaken the explanation that official failures are caused by unreachable targets or a generally weak actuator, and make braking/settling under 50 Hz action updates the leading physical capability concern. They do not establish closed-loop success: the torque probes were short and open-loop, did not use target-directed control, and did not measure tolerance interruptions or endpoint velocity during a hold. Branch selection remains consequential because 5.56% of sampled nominal branches were invalid and margins are angle-dependent. The omitted inner-radius training range, hidden hold phase, and actual learned-policy behavior remain untested. Thus the model's broad-reach consequence is supported, its stabilization concern is strengthened but not proven, and no claim about the 98% objective is yet justified.
request.decision_frontier: Does a policy trained on the full official target distribution achieve reliable uninterrupted holds, with failures primarily caused by post-entry velocity/overshoot and branch execution rather than target infeasibility? Discriminating evidence is a fresh candidate's official-range or task-reference evaluation stratified by radius and angle, together with first-entry time, maximum held steps, interruptions, timeout, and phase-aligned endpoint/joint velocity and action diagnostics. A sharp inner-radius deficit would prioritize distribution coverage; angle-localized failures near low branch margins would prioritize branch-aware control; high first-entry but low hold completion would prioritize braking and stabilization; broad timeout failures would prioritize maneuver horizon or temporal control.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. M1 establishes the physical feasibility and actuation context needed to choose a learned-policy experiment that measures complete holds rather than first reach.
request.next_direction_or_closure: End startup with this checkpoint, then in goal review open a bounded inquiry around full-distribution learned-policy capability. The first inquiry operation should train a fresh policy on the official radius range or otherwise produce a directly comparable policy candidate, followed by diagnostics that distinguish reach, maneuver timeout, branch/limit effects, and uninterrupted hold failure before selecting an intervention.
request.next_question: Can a fresh policy trained on the full official radius distribution reliably convert the measured torque authority into uninterrupted 2-second holds, and are its failures concentrated in inner-radius/angle/branch geometries or in post-entry settling?

request.description: Specialize the transferred full-range policy on the outer official radius band from 0.14 m to 0.20 m.
request.rationale: M3 shows 78 of 80 failures are maneuver timeouts at radii 0.14-0.20 m, while the transferred policy already succeeds on 110 of 113 inner-band episodes and has only two post-entry failures overall. Concentrating training on the failed outer band tests whether the dominant deficit is hard-case allocation and maneuver learning rather than settling, branch feasibility, or insufficient hold shaping. The candidate will be evaluated on the unchanged full official distribution to measure any tradeoff against retained inner-band capability.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO policy with full official radius and angle support while oversampling the timeout-prone outer radius band in 25% of training episodes.
request.rationale: M3 showed that T1's dominant deficit was outer-band maneuver timeout: 78 of 80 failures occurred at radii 0.14-0.20 m, while post-entry failures were only 2 episodes. M5 showed that T2's outer-only transfer was harmful: it reduced inner-band success, introduced 20 post-entry failures with repeated interruptions, and created severe angle-localized failures without solving the timeout problem. The next discriminating intervention preserves the full official support and uniform angle distribution, adds only a bounded 25% outer-band oversampling, and uses fresh initialization to isolate distribution design from the rejected transfer dynamics. Evaluation with restored phase-aligned diagnostics will test outer timeout reduction against inner-band retention and hold stability.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO policy with the T3 full-radius recipe and 50% oversampling of the seam-adjacent target-angle sectors above 135 degrees in absolute value.
request.rationale: M7 shows that T3's residual failures are dominated by maneuver timeouts (56 of 59 failures), concentrated in the -180 to -135 degree sector (26 timeouts and 20% success) and the 135 to 180 degree sector (24 timeouts and 0% success), with a secondary deficit for targets whose best branch margin is 20-40 degrees. Post-entry settling accounts for only 3 failures, so stabilization is not the next intervention. The observation already exposes both analytic IK branch errors; this bounded training change tests whether the failure concentration is primarily insufficient learning exposure to the seam-adjacent branch/angle geometries. Full official radius support and T3's 25% outer-radius oversampling are retained to avoid repeating T2's coverage loss. Evaluation of this candidate on the same rich diagnostics will distinguish improved angle coverage from persistent representation or branch-execution failure.

request.description: Evaluate T4:checkpoint-120832 on a fresh 200-episode full-range research panel with the established hold, geometry, timeout, velocity, and action diagnostics.
request.rationale: T4 was designed to test whether the T3 timeout concentration near the angle seam was caused by insufficient training exposure. Its training log shows no completed training successes, so training statistics cannot establish whether the intervention helped or failed. A behavioral evaluation is the discriminating next operation: the established evaluator will measure uninterrupted hold success and allocate failures by angle, radius, branch-limit margin, maneuver timeout, and post-entry settling. The panel starts at seed 103000 to avoid overlap with the T1 and T3 development panels. If seam-angle timeouts improve without broad coverage loss, angle exposure is supported; if T4 remains broadly unsuccessful or shifts failures into other geometries, the next direction should address the observation/control representation rather than further sampling changes.

request.reason: M9 shows that T4's 50% seam-angle oversampling caused broad competence collapse rather than solving the targeted timeout mechanism: success fell from T3's 70.5% to 18%, with 107 maneuver timeouts and 57 post-entry failures. T4 degraded all ordinary angle sectors, including 0-45 degrees at 6.1% success and 45-90 degrees at 0%, while its hold-phase speeds and actions were near zero because the policy commonly failed to produce useful motion. Restore T3's full-radius recipe with 25% outer-radius oversampling and uniform angle sampling as the validated baseline before changing observation or control representation.
